handling.escalation_reason: One clarifying round is the tenant's limit and the facts needed to act are still missing.

rationale: The triage label describes the opening message, where the missing facts are real and unanswered (G2, G7). What moves is the handling: max_clarify_rounds is 1 for this tenant, the round has been spent, and the answer added nothing, so the next step is a person and not a second question (G5). He cannot send mail at all and has no workaround, so P2. Case-020 and case-022 also spend the round and also expect the escalation, but neither names the rule, and `rules` is scored only where a case states it — so until this one, nothing checked the rule that stops a polite agent asking forever. Naming it turned up why: it cannot fire today. Intake deliberately does not re-enqueue triage for a reply on an existing thread, so the agent is invoked once per ticket, sees clarify_count 0, and always takes the asking branch. The harness models that faithfully and reports reply_routes_to_human here, so expect this case's rule check to fail for as long as that holds. The expectation is what should happen, not what does (G12): the day an agent reads replies, this ticket must escalate rather than ask a second time, and this is the case that says so. Note also what the finding means for the setting — with max_clarify_rounds at 1 or more the second branch is unreachable, and at 0 the agent never asks at all, so today the dial has two positions rather than four.
